links.outcome: Answer quality (accuracy, safety, completeness) of RAG-grounded versus baseline LLM answers to guideline questions
links.effect: RAG significantly outperformed baseline across all criteria (p<0.001) per LLM judge; rheumatologists confirmed for accuracy, safety, completeness (p<0.001); RAG preferred in 92.8% of LLM-judge and 71.2%-74.8% of human comparisons.
links.quote: Analysis revealed that the RAG system significantly outperformed the baseline system across all criteria (p<0.001) in the LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

unlisted_practices: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation of generative AI outputs

screen.reason: The study directly tests and compares LLM output quality (safety, accuracy, completeness) with vs. without retrieval grounding (RAG) added to an existing LLM on clinical guideline questions.
